title: RouteReceipt
description: Route Receipt (MODEL-SWITCHING-SCORECARD.md §40). NOT a standalone file or artifact: this schema describes the `data` object of the append-only ledger envelope event `route.selected` (ARTIBOT-5.0-DESIGN.md §8.2 §3·§40 — 'Route Receipt = 원장 route.selected 이벤트의 data. 별도 파일 아님'). One receipt per routing decision: score per action, switch per epoch (§29). In Phase 0 (Observe) only decision.type 'pin' and 'route' occur — 'switch' is Canary-gated (PRD §3), so a Phase 0 receipt records the recommendation plus the ESTIMATED switch economics with no behaviour change. Field alignment is fixed by lane 2 §4.5 (v5-lane2-routing.md): predicted{} is the route-scorer output, terms{} carries the seven §28 SwitchCost terms each with an explicit measured flag, transition.handoff_tokens is in TOKENS (handoff-builder.js measures bytes — a writer must convert, never store bytes here), routing_epoch_id equals the spawn run_id (G1), and actionsSinceSwitch is the residency/cooldown counter. additionalProperties is false at every level so a typo such as handoff_bytes is rejected rather than silently stored.

schema_version.description: Receipt schema revision. Bumped only on a breaking field change.

route_receipt_id.description: Unique id of this routing decision record.

project_id.description: Optional. Absent in Phase 0, where no project registry has landed yet.

mission_id.description: Mission this decision belongs to (the id from the ledger's mission.created event).

session_id.description: Claude Code session that produced the decision.

task_id.description: Optional. Task the action belongs to; absent when routing happens outside a task.

action_id.description: Optional. Action being scored. Transcript entries carry no action id (lane 2 §2.4), so attribution below spawn granularity is not always available.

intent_revision.description: Optional. Monotonic intent revision the decision was made under.

execution_profile_version.description: Monotonic execution-profile revision (lane 2 §4.5: profile_version increments together with intent_revision). Typed as a counter, not a date string.

routing_epoch_id.description: Routing Epoch (§29) this decision belongs to. Lane 2 §4.5 (G1): the epoch is the spawn, so this equals the spawn run_id and joins to AttemptReceipt.run_id.

action.description: Action classification (§40). Lane 2 §4.5: phase is derived from the resolveModel role (build/review/…), complexity is the classifier score, uncertainty and risk are classifyComplexity.factors passed through. uncertainty and risk are optional because a classifier path may not produce those factors; type, phase and complexity always exist.

type.description: Action class (actionClass) from action-classifier.js, as a CLOSED allowlist of the eight behaviour aliases (lane 2 §2.2, v5-lane2-routing.md:57). A ninth class is a schema change, not a free-form string. Which TIER each class resolves to is a policy decision owned by the T-27 action-classifier and the model-policy config — never by this schema. A receipt records the class that was observed; the same class may resolve to a different tier under a different policy, and models.selected is what actually ran.

phase.description: Lifecycle phase derived from the resolveModel role (e.g. build, review).

models.description: Exact model identities (§20). current is explicitly nullable — the first decision of a session has no incumbent — but the key stays required so 'no incumbent' is recorded rather than omitted. In Observe, recommended and selected differ whenever the router disagrees with policy; that divergence rate is the Phase 0 metric (PRD S3).

current.description: Model in force before this decision, or null when there is none.

recommended.description: What the router recommends (lane 2 §4.5: adaptive-model-router output gains model: ModelIdentity).

selected.description: What was actually used. In Observe this is always the resolveModel policy result, never the recommendation.

decision.description: Lane 2 §4.5: the five-value decision vocabulary is the model-switcher.js output. The legacy reason vocabulary (profile_change | health) is demoted to an entry in reason[], never a decision type.

type.description: §40 decision vocabulary as an allowlist: a value outside these five is rejected rather than passed through.

predicted.description: Route-scorer prediction terms (§40). Lane 2 §4.5: before Shadow these are constants; the fact that they are unmeasured is carried by terms{}.measured rather than duplicated here.

cost.description: Predicted cost in the same unit as AttemptReceipt.cost.total (the null-cost pricing caveat applies).

transition.description: Projection of the switch economics onto the §40 transition block (lane 2 §4.5: mapped from the hysteresis terms).

context_rebuild_tokens.description: Tokens needed to rebuild context after the transition.

cache_loss_estimate.description: Estimated prompt-cache value lost by the transition.

handoff_tokens.description: Handoff size in TOKENS, not bytes. handoff-builder.js measures bytes only (lane 2 §2.5 lists Handoff token attribution as 불가), so a writer must convert; storing a byte count here is a defect.

predicted_time_ms.description: Predicted transition wall time. Unmeasured until a latency input exists — see terms.handoffLatency.measured.

terms.description: The seven §28 SwitchCost terms, key names fixed by lane 2 §4.5. camelCase here because these are the route-hysteresis module's own term names, unlike the snake_case §40 receipt fields. Every term carries measured:boolean so an estimate can never be read as a measurement — before the usage receipt lands, handoffLatency, reorientationRisk and expectedRetry are measured:false (§8.2 R2).

actionsSinceSwitch.description: Residency/cooldown counter feeding §30 minimum_residency and cooldown. Lane 2 §4.5: an epoch is a spawn, so in Phase 0 this counts spawns since the last switch. camelCase follows the hysteresis module contract, matching terms{}.

reason.description: Ordered reason codes for the decision (§40 reason[]). The legacy profile_change and health values live here, not in decision.type. May be empty.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 instant the decision was taken.

source.description: Provenance of the line. Optional: an absent source means production, so every existing production writer stays valid. A shadow line is what the Observe→Shadow learner appends BESIDE the production line (design §3.6, ARTIBOT-5.0-DESIGN.md §3.6 — route.selected{source:'shadow', shadow_of}); the production line is never modified, and a shadow line never changes behaviour.

shadow_of.description: Which production line this shadow line mirrors: the ledger seq or event id of that line. Required when source is shadow (see allOf below) — a shadow line that names no original cannot be paired for counterfactual comparison, which is the only thing shadow lines exist for. Must be absent-or-meaningless for production lines, which name no original.

model_identity.description: Exact model identity (§20, §42). Duplicated verbatim in attempt-receipt.schema.json; the T-19 common meta fragment is the intended future home. version (not the §20 spelling snapshot_or_version) is the canonical key — lane 2 §4.5 flags that document inconsistency and resolves it in favour of §42.

provider.description: e.g. anthropic. Left a free string: the field exists precisely because a non-Anthropic provider is possible (§59 vLLM reference).

tier.description: Artibot tier alias. Allowlist grounded in the lib/core/model-catalog.js MODELS keys (measured 2026-09-02: haiku, sonnet, opus, fable).

model_id.description: Exact provider model id from model-catalog.js (e.g. claude-fable-5-1), never the tier alias.

version.description: Provider snapshot/version string for the model id.

catalog_version.description: Version of the Artibot model catalog the identity was resolved against. PREREQUISITE: lib/core/model-catalog.js exports no CATALOG_VERSION today (repo-wide grep 0 excluding node_modules, measured 2026-09-02), so that constant must be added before a writer can populate this field.

cost_term.description: One §28 SwitchCost term. measured is mandatory so estimated and measured terms are never conflated (§46 EXACT/PARTIAL/SIMULATED labelling).

value.description: Term magnitude in the term's own unit (tokens, currency, or a 0..1 risk weight).

measured.description: true only when the value came from an actual measurement. Constants and heuristics are false.
